findings.why_it_matters: A space was inserted into the PICTURE character-string. In COBOL a space terminates the PICTURE character-string, so the transcribed line is not the same source: it reads as PICTURE '$$$,$$$.' followed by a stray '99.' rather than the six-digit floating-dollar edited item with two decimal places that the example (a packed-decimal print method) is illustrating. Verified by cropping and zooming the 300dpi render of the line; the printed glyphs are contiguous with no space between '.' and '99'.
findings.suggested_repair: Restore the line to '01  Out-p pic $$$,$$$.99.' (no space before the 99).

findings.pdf_says: D.19.5.4.2  Class polymorphism  /  D.19.5.4.3  Parametric polymorphism (both are fourth-level subclauses of D.19.5.4 Polymorphism, whose first subclause D.19.5.4.1 General is transcribed as '### D.19.5.4.1 General')
findings.markdown_says: ## D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism  ...  ## D.19.5.4.3 Parametric polymorphism
findings.why_it_matters: Both subclauses are emitted at the same markdown level (##) as their own parent '## D.19.5.4 Polymorphism' and one level above their sibling '### D.19.5.4.1 General', so the outline makes them peers of D.19.5.4 instead of its children. Any TOC, anchor-nav or section-scoped tooling built over the markdown reports the wrong containment for these clauses. The transcription's own convention (first sibling nested, later siblings flattened) is visible throughout Annex D - e.g. D.18.2.1 is ###, D.18.2.2/D.18.2.3 are ##; D.20.3.1/D.20.3.2 are ####, D.20.3.3/D.20.3.4/D.20.3.5 are ## - which proves the flattening is a tool artifact, not an editorial choice.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote both to '### D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism' and '### D.19.5.4.3 Parametric polymorphism' to match the sibling D.19.5.4.1.
